# Donald Trump

Donald Trump is an American businessman, television personality, and politician. Born in 1946, he rose to fame as a real estate magnate and entrepreneur, known for his brand and iconic Trump Tower in New York City. In 2016, Trump, a Republican, became the 45th President of the United States after a divisive and controversial campaign.

passages.heading: US 'needs to get idea of bringing us to our knees out of its head', says Iran
passages.text:
## US 'needs to get idea of bringing us to our knees out of its head', says Iran

President Masoud Pezeshkian has said Iran will continue to defend itself but remains open to discussions with America.

According to state media, he said that the US needed to “get the idea of bringing us to our knees with terror and martyrdom out of its head.”

Pezeshkian added: “We defend the rights of our society with dignity and pride, and we have never run away from dialogue and will not do so, although the United States has targeted our country three times despite having signed the agreement.

“The enemies thought that with the martyrdom of the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Revolution, the people, commanders, and scientists - the country - would collapse, but our national and internal unity and cohesion increased.”

passages.heading: Live war map
passages.text:
# Live war map

**A world map of conflict that redraws itself as the news arrives.** Every country carries a live 0–100 safety score, and every confirmed strike of the last 24 hours is marked where it happened.

- **3** Active conflict zones on the map
- **8** Strike markers on the map
- **233** Countries and territories on the map

Colour runs from dark red (extremely dangerous, 0–30) through amber to green (very safe, 85–100). The bands are fixed, so a country changing colour means its score crossed a threshold, not that the scale moved.

passages.heading: Live war map
passages.text: A country only gets markers once two independent models have confirmed military action on its territory from two separate reports; the markers themselves are the individual located reports behind that. They fade out as the 24-hour window closes, while the underlying score recovers far more slowly — which is why a country can be red with no markers on it. See the methodology for the exact rules.

passages.heading: Questions
passages.text:
- What wars are active right now?
- 3, as of the timestamp above: Palestine, Russia, Ukraine. This counts countries with combat on their own territory confirmed by two independent models within the last 24 hours, not declared wars.
- How many wars are going on today?
- As of 1 October 2026, 3 countries have confirmed active combat on their own territory: Palestine, Russia, Ukraine. This counts countries with confirmed fighting in the last 24 hours, not declared wars, so a single conflict involving two countries appears as two entries.
- Where can I see a world map of the most dangerous countries?
- This page is that map. Every country and territory is shaded by its live 0–100 safety index, so the darkest areas are the most dangerous ones right now, and the ranked table version is at /most-dangerous-countries.
- What does the live war map show?
- Every country and territory shaded by its current safety index from 0 to 100, with a blast marker at the location of each confirmed strike from the last 24 hours. Disputed territories are hatched rather than coloured, because assigning them to one claimant would be an editorial call the data cannot support.
- How often does the map update?
- Continuously. New articles are read and scored around the clock, and the map re-renders as soon as a score or a strike changes — typically within minutes of a report appearing.
- Where does the data come from?
- Public news feeds and public Telegram channels, read by independent AI models that classify each report by country, threat category and severity.
